actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository implements a convex model predictive controller for the Unitree Go2 quadruped, including contact-force optimization, centroidal linearized dynamics, Raibert-style foot planning, swing-leg path generation and MuJoCo simulation
The upstream MuJoCo model class resolves models/MJCF/go2/scene.xml and loads it with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path, then creates its data with mujoco.MjData
The primary scene is the MJCF model 'go2 scene' and includes go2.xml from the same directory
The scene adds a floor plane, two low boxes and a rising row of boxes along the x axis
The robot model is named go2, is compiled in radians with meshdir assets and autolimits, and sets the elliptic friction cone with impratio 100
The quadruped root body base_link is at z=0.445 m and is attached to the world by a freejoint
The go2 default class gives its motor elements the control range -23.7 to 23.7
The knee default class overrides the motor control range to -45.43 to 45.43
The joint ranges are abduction -1.0472 to 1.0472 rad, front hip -1.5708 to 3.4907 rad, back hip -0.5236 to 4.5379 rad and knee -2.7227 to -0.83776 rad
The actuator block declares 12 motor actuators, one hip, thigh and calf per leg, named in FR, FL, RR and RL order
The model provides a home keyframe with 19 qpos values (a floating base plus 12 joints) and 12 ctrl values
The sensor section declares joint position, velocity and actuator force sensors for all 12 joints, plus IMU orientation, gyroscope, accelerometer, position and linear velocity at the imu site
The demos run the simulation at SIM_HZ 1000 with SIM_DT 1/1000 s
The demos assign SIM_DT to model.opt.timestep before the simulation loop
The demo loop advances each physics step with mj_step1, writes the held joint torques through set_joint_torque, then calls mj_step2
The model wrapper looks up each leg's hip, thigh and calf actuator ids by name and writes torque[0], torque[1] and torque[2] to data.ctrl
set_joint_torque assigns the 12-value torque vector in FL, FR, RL, RR leg order
The second scene, scene_terrain.xml, includes go2.xml and adds two height fields and obstacle geometry; this package serves the primary scene.xml
The package requires Python 3.10 or newer below 3.11
The README recommends Linux for the project and states that other operating systems were not tested

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one loaded MJCF deterministically from the reset state and the model has no random element; the bridge accepts a reset seed for the class contract but mj_resetData does not use it.  The package's fake is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses scene.xml and its included go2.xml for the 19 qpos and 18 dof coordinates, the 12 motor actuators and their ctrlranges, then moves each actuated hinge a placeholder fraction toward its control value; it computes no inertias, contacts, friction, actuator or sensor dynamics and was never compared with the engine

the model file sets no <option timestep>; the published timestep_ms 2.0 is the fake's placeholder for MuJoCo's library default, while the upstream demos set model.opt.timestep to 1 ms (examples/ex00_demo.py:83-85,185-186), so the step used by a real bridge load of the raw scene is not verified here

the bridge's ctrl vector order is the model actuator order FR, FL, RR, RL (models/MJCF/go2/go2.xml:222-235), while the upstream set_joint_torque maps the 12-value vector in FL, FR, RL, RR order (src/convex_mpc/mujoco_model.py:41-46); a client must reorder, and the upstream MPC, gait and leg controllers are not served

the bridge's reset calls mj_resetData and starts from the model defaults; the fake starts every array at zero, while the model's base_link default is z=0.445 m (models/MJCF/go2/go2.xml:64) and the home keyframe is not applied

the stand-in loads no mesh or texture (the model's asset section names 16 OBJ files under assets/) and resolves no contact, friction, sensor or actuator dynamics; a real engine load needs the meshes beside the model, which the pinned clone provides
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the model step only; the upstream demo's render pacing and replay viewer are not used
no rendering, cameras or sensor publication: the model's 36 joint sensors and five IMU sensors are not exposed; the observation is only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl state
only the card's primary scene is served; the terrain scene scene_terrain.xml and the URDF description are not loaded by this package
no physical Go2 is modelled or controlled and nothing was validated against the robot; MuJoCo itself was not installed where the gate ran, so no trajectory here is an engine result

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
